note: One expectation index per contract directory. Each case names the structural violations that prove its point as (pointer, keyword) pairs; a validator's free-text message is deliberately never recorded. The expected set must be a subset of what the validator reports, because a conditional rule often reports a broader violation alongside the specific one.

gate-family-missing.proves: Every one of the seven gate families is reported. A receipt that drops a gate could make a run look releasable by omission.

gate-family-unknown.proves: The gate families are closed at the seven of validation v1. A gate a later capability needs arrives with a contract version, never as an unrecognised member.

gate-state-unknown.proves: The gate state vocabulary is closed at PASS, FAIL, BLOCKED and NOT_APPLICABLE; there is no fifth, softer state to hide a problem in.

gate-state-lowercase.proves: The gate state vocabulary is case-sensitive, so a lowercased token cannot be matched against an approved state by accident.

overall-not-applicable.proves: NOT_APPLICABLE is neutral and describes a gate, never the validation as a whole.

pass-overall-for-failed-run.proves: Only a run that succeeded may pass validation: a run that did not execute to the end has nothing to release.

pass-overall-without-run-state.proves: A passing validation states the run state it passed on, so SUCCEEDED can be read off the receipt rather than assumed.

pass-gate-with-reason.proves: A passing gate names no problem: a gate cannot hold while giving a reason it does not.

fail-gate-without-reason.proves: A failing gate names the defect it failed on; an unexplained FAIL could not be acted on.

fail-gate-with-only-blocked-reasons.proves: FAIL is reserved for defects of this service. A gate whose only reasons are missing evidence is BLOCKED, never FAIL, so a technical limitation can never be escalated into a defect.

blocked-gate-with-fail-reason.proves: A BLOCKED gate names BLOCKED reasons only: a defect cannot be softened into a limitation.

blocked-gate-without-reason.proves: A blocked gate states what is missing; an unexplained BLOCKED is not a limitation anyone can resolve.

not-applicable-gate-with-two-reasons.proves: A gate that does not apply says why exactly once.

not-applicable-gate-with-blocked-reason.proves: An exemption is not a limitation: a NOT_APPLICABLE gate cannot carry a BLOCKED reason, which would state a problem while declaring the gate irrelevant.

reason-code-website-quality.proves: The reason vocabulary is closed, so no reason describing the website can arrive: every BLOCKED reason names our process.

reason-carries-a-message.proves: A reason carries tokens and a location only. Free text could carry a validator's message or website content into a document every adapter renders.

reasons-duplicated.proves: A reason is reported once, so a count of reasons is a count of problems.

customer-release-property.proves: Run validation is not a customer-release decision; SUCCEEDED and a passing validation together still decide no release.

score-property.proves: A receipt carries no score: validation says whether a result can be relied on, never how good the website is.

bundle-digest-uppercase.proves: One bundle has exactly one written digest: upper-case hexadecimal is refused.

run-state-unknown.proves: The run state is copied from the run's own vocabulary, never paraphrased.
